verdict.line: You lose if Darius lands E (Apprehend) and stacks Hemorrhage to 5 before your Fury builds; you win by trading Q-sustain while his E is down.

brief.thesis: This is a genuinely even lane (47.7% win rate over 961 games, even lane and solo-kill advantage) decided by whose cooldown is up first: Darius needs E (Apprehend) live to force a fight and stack Hemorrhage to max, while Renekton needs 50+ Fury for empowered Q and W before committing. The 2026 skill order (QEWQQR...) delays your W to rank 1 until roughly level 14, so early trades are won with Q sustain and E poke, not stun-locks.

theirWindow.what: Once he pulls you in, his passive Hemorrhage stacks climb fast and his Q (Decimate) heals him off the blade edge — back off or Flash immediately rather than trading through it, especially once he's 5-stacked and enraged.

yourWindow.what: With his hook down he can't force range, so walk up and trade freely — hold your all-in until you're above 50 Fury so W (Ruthless Predator) hits the 3-slash, shield-destroying, 1.5s stun version instead of the weak 0.75s single-stun version.

start.why: 80.4% pick rate and the higher win rate of the two starts (48.5% over 965 games) — the extra AD helps you win the auto-attack exchanges Darius wants to force with his passive bleed.

boots.why: 85.5% pick rate at 49.4% win rate — Darius lives on autos and Q, so flat physical damage reduction blunts every trade he starts.

core.why: Shared first item on the two highest-win-rate paths (60.7% and 58.2%) — the shield lets you tank his all-in commitment while your empowered abilities land.
Second item on both top paths — the armor shred stacks with your empowered E's own Armor reduction, compounding your damage in extended fights.
Highest win rate completed path (60.7% over 140 games) — the damage-over-time conversion directly counters Darius's Hemorrhage bleed stacking on you.

situational.when: the enemy team has burst that threatens to delete you right after your all-in commits
you're ahead and want your ability haste and Fury generation to snowball faster
you need the extra mobility and wave clear to reset side lane after trades
the enemy team stacks hard CC or magic damage worth swapping your boots for

runes.keystoneWhy: Higher win rate and pick rate than Press the Attack here (46.5% vs 44.3%) — Conqueror's stacking heal matches Renekton's Q sustain in the extended fights this lane produces, rather than rewarding a single burst window like Darius wants.

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite is run in 92.8% of games at 48.2% win rate — Ignite cuts off the healing from Darius's Q (Decimate) blade hits during your Fury-empowered all-in, denying his best sustain tool exactly when you commit.

playing.title: Engage only above 50 Fury
playing.detail: Below 50 Fury your W (Ruthless Predator) is a single 0.75s stun; above it, it becomes a 3-hit, shield-destroying, 1.5s stun. Wait for the threshold before starting your all-in combo.

playing.title: Trade when his E is down
playing.detail: Darius's E (Apprehend) is his only way to force range, on a 26/23.5/21/18.5/16s cooldown. Walk up and poke with Q (Cull the Meek, 7s cooldown) whenever you've seen him use it.

playing.title: Watch his Hemorrhage stack count
playing.detail: His passive bleeds you for 5 seconds per stack and enrages him at max stacks (5) with a large AD boost. Disengage before he reaches that threshold rather than fighting through it.

playing.title: Dodge the blade edge of his Q
playing.detail: Decimate deals more damage and heals him only on the outer blade hit. Standing at melee range against him minimizes both his damage and his sustain from it.

playing.title: Don't overcommit E
playing.detail: Slice and Dice is your only gap closer and escape, on a 16-10s cooldown depending on rank. Use it to engage or disengage, never both in the same trade.

playing.title: Lean on Q, not W, before level 14
playing.detail: The 2026 skill order maxes Q and E first and leaves W at rank 1 until roughly level 14, so your stun is weak for most of laning — win trades with Q sustain and auto-attacks instead of chaining stuns.

playing.title: Ignite the all-in, not the poke
playing.detail: Save Ignite for when you're already committed to a kill attempt with Fury up, since it removes his Q heal and any regen he'd use to survive your burst.

brief.patchCaveat: The build, runes, boots, summoners, and win-rate figures above are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch (16.18.1); the tactical reading of Fury thresholds, cooldown windows, and trade patterns is my own analysis layered on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Bring Ignite and wait for Renekton’s Fury to build up before engaging. Avoid being hit at the tip of Darius’s (Q).
